preamble: Vocalization of a voiced velar stop before a consonant to a high front vocoid, the offglide [i̯] of a new diphthong. In western Romance, Latin g before r or n weakened and vocalized, so that nigrum gave Old French neir (French noir), integrum gave Old Galician-Portuguese enteiro and rēgnum gave reino. A fricative stage [ɣ] is often assumed but is not attested. It parallels the vocalization of k in clusters such as Latin -ct- > Portuguese -it-.

examples.note: g before r vocalized to the glide [i̯]

examples.to: Old French flairier, French flairer (to smell, sniff)

sources: Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511845192
